# A mixed-plus-own-depth envelope with actual midpoint slab charges

This note introduces a scalar parameter only to select actual points of
the original mixed set. Its inequalities retain actual ambient critical
caps and actual measured slabs. It proves no OC coverage inequality and
does not assume that a sum of quasiconcave and concave functions is
quasiconcave.

## 1. Definitions, attainment, and the archived own-depth concavity

Let C be a convex body in R^n times R^d with d>=1 and positive mixed
d-volume. Let mu be the sum of ordinary d-volume over its finitely many
integer fibers. Write S=C intersect (Z^n times R^d) and M=mu(S).
For Y=(z,x) in S define

    D(Y)=inf_{closed ambient H containing Y} mu(H),
    f(Y)=ordinary raw depth of x in C_z,
    F(Y)=f(Y)^(1/d).

Put f=F=0 on fibers of zero d-volume. Their mixed depth is also zero,
by the proved intrinsic finite-base own-depth upper-bound theorem. The
same theorem excludes fiber-boundary points from positive mixed depth.

On every positive fiber D and f are continuous. For D this follows from
the general finite-base normalized-continuous-normal attainment and
uniform slab bound proved in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`; its base
set is arbitrary finite P in R^n. For f the ordinary compact-sphere cap
argument gives continuity. Consequently every maximization below is
attained on the finite union of compact positive fibers. Its maximum is
positive, since an own-fiber centroid has positive own and mixed depth.
All selected maximizers are interior to their positive fibers.

The ordinary own-depth root is jointly concave on C. Explicitly, for
Y_t=(1-t)Y_0+tY_1, every common continuous direction u has the inclusion

    (1-t)[C_(z0) intersect {u.X>=u.x0}]
       +t[C_(z1) intersect {u.X>=u.x1}]
       subset C_(zt) intersect {u.X>=u.xt}.

BM and then the infimum over u give

    F(Y_t)>=(1-t)F(Y_0)+tF(Y_1).                         (1)

This is the archived joint own-depth theorem, not a new principle here.
Its inequality is used only at actual integer midpoints below.

For lambda>=0 define

    P_lambda(Y)=D(Y)+lambda F(Y),
    E(lambda)=max_(Y in S) P_lambda(Y),
    Q=E(0)=max_S D,
    Fmax=max_S F,
    Fstar=max{F(Y):D(Y)=Q}.

In particular Fstar>0 and Q>0. No quasiconcavity or parity-count bound
for P_lambda is claimed.

## 2. Exact two-parameter exchange and envelope work

Suppose lambda0<lambda1 and Y_i maximizes P_(lambda_i). Write
D_i=D(Y_i),F_i=F(Y_i),delta=F_1-F_0,A=D_0-D_1. Comparing each selected
point in the other parameter's objective gives exactly

    delta>=0,   lambda0 delta<=A<=lambda1 delta.         (2)

If delta=0, then A=0. Thus selected own-depth roots increase with the
parameter, while selected actual mixed depths decrease. Equation (2)
holds for any selections at distinct parameters. At one parameter,
order tied maximizers by F; their D values then decrease with exact
rate lambda.

The envelope E is convex and Fmax-Lipschitz, because it is the maximum
of affine functions of slopes in [0,Fmax]. Let F(lambda) be the LARGEST
F among its actual maximizing sources, and put

    D(lambda)=E(lambda)-lambda F(lambda).

Both quantities are realized by one actual maximizing source at each
lambda. The selected points need not form a continuous or measurable
path; the scalar F(lambda) is enough. It is monotone and right-continuous.
For the latter assertion take parameters decreasing to lambda and actual
maximizers realizing the largest active slopes. Compactness supplies a
limit source active at lambda. Its F is the limit of the slopes and
cannot exceed the largest active F there; monotonicity gives the reverse
inequality. This also proves F(0)=Fstar. Equivalently E'_+(lambda)=F(lambda):
for h>0, the difference quotient of E lies between F(lambda) and
F(lambda+h), by the two maximizing comparisons.

For 0<=a<b the exact identity is

    D(a)-D(b)=integral_(a,b] lambda dF(lambda).           (3)

The integral is the Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral for the bounded monotone
right-continuous F. A complete direct proof uses finite partitions:
(2) places each actual mixed-depth drop between the corresponding lower
and upper sums of lambda times the slope increment. Summing telescopes
the actual D drops. The two sums differ by at most the mesh times
F(b)-F(a), which tends to zero. The interval excludes an atom at a and
includes one at b, matching the right-continuous endpoint convention.
In particular

    Q-D(b)=integral_(0,b] lambda dF(lambda).              (4)

For every positive parameter and every active source,

    Fstar<=F(Y)<=Fmax,
    Q-lambda(Fmax-Fstar)<=D(Y)<=Q.                      (5)

These follow by comparing with a deepest point realizing Fstar.

There is also an exact total budget. Let

    Dtop=max{D(Y):F(Y)=Fmax}.

Then F(lambda) tends to Fmax and D(lambda) tends to Dtop as lambda
tends to infinity, and hence

    integral_(0,infinity) lambda dF(lambda)=Q-Dtop.      (6)

Indeed comparison with a source attaining Dtop at Fmax gives
D(lambda)>=Dtop+lambda(Fmax-F(lambda)), while D(lambda)<=Q; thus
Fmax-F(lambda)<=Q/lambda. Any subsequential limit source is on F=Fmax,
so continuity bounds its mixed depth by Dtop. Since D(lambda) is
monotone, its limit is Dtop. Monotone convergence in (4) proves (6).
Also Dtop>=Fmax^d from its own fiber, so this total budget is at most
Q-Fmax^d. It is an actual loss of mixed depth, not a fiber-volume sum.

## 3. Integer midpoint geometry and the exact slab

Let Y0,Y1 be distinct active sources at parameters lambda0<=lambda1,
with lambda1>0. When the parameters are equal, order the sources so that
F1>=F0. Suppose their integer bases have the same parity. Their midpoint
Ym belongs to S by actual convexity, and (1) gives

    Delta=F(Ym)-(F0+F1)/2>=0.                            (7)

Let H be ANY depth-attaining cap through Ym, chosen with nonzero
continuous normal and normalized as

    H={L>=0},
    L(z,x)=a.(z-zm)+u.(x-xm), |u|=1.

Such a finite attaining cap exists, because Ym is interior to its
positive fiber. Its mass is Dm=D(Ym). If an endpoint Ye has nonnegative
margin s=L(Ye), define the actual whole mixed slab

    T_H=mu{0<=L<s}.

The parallel shifted cap {L>=s} contains Ye. Its boundary is null in
every positive d-dimensional fiber, so exactly

    Dm-mu{L>=s}=T_H,   Dm>=D_e+T_H.                     (8)

If s>0 then T_H>0: the endpoint's own fiber contains a ball around Ye,
and a positive part of that ball lies in the removed slab. No volume is
silently assigned to a different candidate point.

## 4. A critical midpoint cap faces the larger-own-depth endpoint

Suppose delta=F1-F0>0. Midpoint optimality at lambda0 gives

    Dm<=D0-lambda0(F(Ym)-F0)
       <=D0-lambda0 delta/2.                            (9)

If lambda0>0 this is strictly less than D0. Thus no critical cap at Ym
can contain Y0, even on its boundary: any cap containing Y0 has mass
at least D0. Consequently every such cap has Y1 STRICTLY inside.
This facing statement follows from the endpoint parameter lambda0;
it is not inferred from the envelope-gap estimate below.

If lambda0=0, (9) gives Dm<=D0. A cap containing Y0 strictly would,
by its positive proper own-fiber slab, have mass strictly greater than
D0, a contradiction. If Y0 is on its boundary, Y1 is also on it.
Thus Y1 still has a nonnegative margin, and can be used in (8).

Optimality at the other endpoint parameter gives the simultaneous exact
bounds

    T_H+lambda0 Delta <= A-lambda0 delta/2,
    T_H+lambda1 Delta <= lambda1 delta/2.                (10)

For lambda0>0 and delta>0 the slab is positive, so Delta<delta/2.
In particular F0<F(Ym)<F1 and D1<Dm<D0 in that case. These inequalities
do not say Ym itself maximizes any P_lambda.

If delta=0, (2) gives A=0. Quasiconcavity of D gives Dm>=D0, and midpoint
optimality at lambda1>0 gives Dm+lambda1 F(Ym)<=D0+lambda1 F0. Therefore
Dm=D0,F(Ym)=F0 and Delta=0. Every critical cap has both endpoints on its
boundary by the positive-slab argument. This is the already understood
exact common-cap/facet-flux regime; no new parity exclusion is inferred.

## 5. An exact envelope-gap charge

First take delta>0 and lambda0<lambda1. Let

    lambda*=A/delta in [lambda0,lambda1],
    B=E(lambda*)-[D0+lambda*F0]>=0.

The two endpoint affine objective lines agree at lambda*. Since Ym is
an actual candidate, Dm+lambda*F(Ym)<=E(lambda*). Together with (8),
using the endpoint Y1 established in Section 4, this gives

    T_H+lambda* Delta <= A/2+B.                          (11)

For auditing the endpoint sign explicitly: if one merely selects an
endpoint Ye with nonnegative margin without the facing proof, the same
calculation gives the right side +A/2+B for e=1 and -A/2+B for e=0.
The upper bound in (11) is valid in either case. The stronger facing
claim uses (9), not an unproved bound B<A/2.

Convexity of E places it below the chord through its two endpoint values.
At lambda* this gives the exact rational-expression bound

    0<=B<=delta (lambda*-lambda0)(lambda1-lambda*)
                         /(lambda1-lambda0)
          <=(lambda1-lambda0)delta/4.                   (12)

The first expression follows by subtracting the common endpoint line
from that chord; the last inequality is the elementary product bound.
The gap B measures intermediate actual candidates that outperform BOTH
endpoint lines. It may not be silently omitted.

If lambda0=lambda1=lambda>0, then A=lambda delta,lambda*=lambda,B=0,
and the exact same-parameter inequality is

    T_H+lambda Delta <= lambda delta/2=A/2.              (13)

If delta=0, set B=0; Delta=T_H=A=0 as proved above, so these budget
statements have their natural zero interpretation without dividing by
delta. A full section can have many P_lambda maximizers; Section 8 gives
an exact continuum, so no finite parity count for them is allowed.

## 6. Quantitative control of the coupled normal by an own-fiber ball

Let Ye be the endpoint with nonnegative margin s in Section 3. Suppose
its own fiber contains a Euclidean ball B(x_e,r), r>0. Since |u|=1,
its contribution alone gives

    T_H>=Psi_(d,r)(s),                                  (14)

where for d>=2

    Psi_(d,r)(s)=kappa_(d-1) integral_0^min(s,r)
                              (r^2-t^2)^((d-1)/2) dt,

and Psi_(1,r)(s)=min(s,r). Here kappa_j is the volume of the unit j-ball,
with kappa_0=1. Formula (14) is simply the exact ball slab between the
endpoint plane and the preceding plane; it keeps every oblique integer
coefficient a unchanged.

Such a radius is supplied explicitly by own depth and a diameter bound.
If the endpoint fiber has diameter R_e>0, every parallel section has
(d-1)-measure at most kappa_(d-1) R_e^(d-1). Its cap above a plane through
x_e is no more than that quantity times the distance to its support
plane, while it is at least f(Ye). Every support distance is therefore
at least

    r=f(Ye)/(kappa_(d-1) R_e^(d-1)),

so the corresponding ball is contained in the fiber. For d=1 the same
formula reads r=f(Ye), as it should.

Put c_r=kappa_(d-1)(sqrt(3)r/2)^(d-1). Then

    Psi_(d,r)(s)>=c_r min(s,r/2).                        (15)

If an upper budget epsilon for T_H, from (10) or (11), satisfies
epsilon<c_r r/2, one obtains s<=epsilon/c_r. Since the two endpoint
margins are opposite, this bounds the FULL coupled normal evaluation

    |a.(z1-z0)+u.(x1-x0)|=2s<=2epsilon/c_r.             (16)

By (5), all positive-parameter selected sources have own depth at least
Fstar^d. A common finite fiber-diameter bound therefore supplies one
positive r for these estimates, independent of lambda. No width or
inradius assumption is added to C; the displayed constant depends on
its actual geometry and is not asserted uniform over all bodies.

## 7. Finite-chain accounting, with all coverage restrictions retained

Take a finite sequence of selected actual sources Y_j at nondecreasing
positive parameters lambda_j<=Lambda, with F_j nondecreasing at tied
parameters. Assume every adjacent base pair has the same parity, so all
these midpoints are actual. For each pair choose ANY actual critical
midpoint cap, and let T_j be its measured slab mass and Delta_j its
own-depth-root midpoint gain. Equations (11)--(12) give

    sum_j [T_j+lambda*_j Delta_j]
      <=(D_0-D_N)/2
             +(1/4)sum_j(lambda_(j+1)-lambda_j)(F_(j+1)-F_j)
      <=(D_0-D_N)/2+eta(F_N-F_0)/4,                    (17)

where eta=max_j(lambda_(j+1)-lambda_j). Zero root increments use the
zero interpretation; tied parameter edges have B=0. The mixed-depth
term telescopes exactly. At a single parameter the error vanishes.
For canonical selections it equals half the corresponding Stieltjes
work integral (3). Thus (17) is not a sum of scalar root moments alone:
it controls actual original-measure slabs and actual root gains.

In particular the measure of the UNION of these slabs is at most their
sum, hence at most the right side of (17). This is an upper budget with
multiplicity already controlled by the displayed inequalities; no
assertion that the slabs are disjoint is required.

One can apply (17) separately to subsequences in each occupied parity.
There are at most 2^n such chains, but eta must then measure successive
parameter gaps WITHIN those subsequences. It need not tend to zero when
the original full parameter sampling becomes fine. Nor is the envelope
gap B necessarily zero across a skipped interval containing other active
sources. These are exact restrictions, not negligible remainder terms.

Most importantly, no proved statement here makes the charged slabs
cover the original source or a fixed fraction of its mass. Without such
an additional geometric covering relation, neither (6) nor (17) gives
OC. No quasiconcavity of P_lambda, finite count of its maximizers, or
unproved simultaneous cap selection is used.

## 8. Exact actual calibration and a continuum of potential maximizers

Take n=d=1 and the convex body

    C={-1<=z<=1, 0<=x<=3-2|z|}.

Its actual interval fibers are [0,1],[0,3],[0,1], with total mass five.
The endpoint fibers can be isolated by finite tilts. At a middle point
x in [0,3], complete all-direction minimization gives

    D(0,x)=min[x+min(2x,1),
                 3-x+min(2(1-x)_+,1)].                 (18)

This exact interval-tail formula is also proved in
`candidate a57c113e8e14cc38`.
For completeness the endpoint clipped pair satisfies
min_a[clip(x+a,0,1)+clip(x-a,0,1)]=min(2x,1) for x>=0:
if x<=1/2 unclipped values attain 2x and clipping cannot lower it;
if x>=1/2 either both are inside and sum to 2x>=1, or one saturates,
and a finite large tilt attains one. Reflection supplies the upward
formula. Pure integer caps have mass four and do not lower (18).

On [1,3/2], the actual mixed depth is D=3-x and the ordinary own depth
is f=F=x. At lambda=1 every point in that entire interval maximizes
P_1 with value three. Indeed for x<=1, D<=x+1 and f<=x, so P_1<=2x+1<=3;
for x>=3/2, D<=3-x and f<=3-x, so P_1<=2(3-x)<=3. Endpoint-fiber
candidates have P_1<=1. Thus one parity class, even one fixed integer
fiber, contains a continuum of potential maximizers.

More precisely

    E(lambda)=max(2+lambda, 3/2+(3/2)lambda).

For 0<=lambda<1 the unique maximizing source is (0,1); for lambda>1
it is (0,3/2); at lambda=1 the displayed interval is the maximizing set.
The same piecewise bounds, or (18), prove these claims. Endpoint-fiber
objectives are at most (1+lambda)/2 and never win.

For Y0=(0,1),Y1=(0,3/2) at the common parameter one, their midpoint
is (0,5/4). The actual critical cap {x>=5/4} has mass 7/4, contains
Y1 at margin 1/4, and shifting it to Y1 removes the actual middle-fiber
slab of mass T=1/4. The own-root midpoint gain is Delta=0, while
A=D0-D1=1/2 and delta=F1-F0=1/2. Hence

    T+lambda Delta=1/4=A/2,

so the exact coefficient one-half in the same-parameter charge is
attained. Splitting the maximizing interval into any finite increasing
sequence gives equality in the sum of these slab charges as well.

The canonical envelope slope jumps from one to 3/2 at lambda=1,
and its mixed-depth intercept jumps from two to 3/2. Equation (6)
therefore reads integral lambda dF=1*(1/2)=1/2=Q-Dtop exactly.
This body has global normalized depth 2/5, above OC's 1/4. It calibrates
the actual charging identities and refutes a finite-maximizer shortcut;
it is not an OC counterexample.

## 9. Ordered actual points along a segment of tied sources

Here is a geometric consequence stronger than a scalar midpoint bound.
Fix lambda>0 and distinct maximizers Y0,Y1 of P_lambda. Suppose
F1>F0, and write delta=F1-F0 and A=D0-D1=lambda delta>0.
For 0<t<1 put Yt=(1-t)Y0+tY1. Retain only those t for which the
integer base of Yt is integral, and include t=0,1. For every such t,
Yt is interior to a positive fiber. Put

    Delta_t=F(Yt)-[(1-t)F0+tF1]>=0.

Every depth-attaining nonvertical cap Ht={Lt>=0} through Yt satisfies

    Lt(Y0)<0<Lt(Y1),                                   (19)
    D1<D(Yt)<D0,   F0<F(Yt)<F1.                        (20)

Indeed the tied endpoint objectives and own-root concavity imply

    D(Yt)<=D0-tA-lambda Delta_t<D0.

Thus Ht cannot contain Y0. Affineness and Lt(Yt)=0 force the strict
positive sign at Y1. Shifting Ht to Y1 removes a positive slab of its
interior positive fiber, so D(Yt)>D1. Comparing the objective at Yt
with the tied objective at Y1 gives F(Yt)<F1; the lower strict bound
follows directly from concavity and delta>0. In particular no such
intermediate point is an ordinary local maximum of actual D on its
own continuous fiber when the endpoints have the same base: every
critical continuous normal has positive dot product with x1-x0.
This last conclusion also follows directly from the strict depth
monotonicity below and does not need a derivative assumption.

If 0<t<s<=1 are two retained parameters, the affine sign calculation
in (19) gives Lt(Ys)>0. Define the actual slab

    T_(t,s)=mu{0<=Lt<Lt(Ys)}.

Then the exact shift argument gives

    0<T_(t,s)<=D(Yt)-D(Ys).                             (21)

Consequently actual mixed depth is strictly decreasing along ALL the
retained actual points of the segment. For the left endpoint the strict
inequality D0>D(Ys) was already proved, so the monotonicity includes
both endpoints. Own-depth root is strictly increasing along these
points. To prove this, if 0<t<s<1 had F(Ys)<=F(Yt), concavity of F on
the continuous segment would give

    [F1-F(Ys)]/(1-s)
        <=[F(Ys)-F(Yt)]/(s-t)<=0,

contradicting F(Ys)<F1. Endpoint comparisons use (20).

The cap at Yt also has the exact remaining-segment budget

    T_(t,1)+lambda Delta_t <=(1-t)A.                    (22)

This is (21) with s=1 combined with the displayed objective bound.
For any finite increasing list of retained parameters strictly above
zero, the adjacent slab charges telescope:

    sum_j T_(t_j,t_(j+1))
         <=D(Y_(t_0))-D(Y_(t_N))<=A.                  (23)

The caps may differ from edge to edge, so (23) asserts an upper budget,
not disjointness or coverage. If the endpoint bases coincide, every
real parameter t is retained; if they differ, only actual integer
parameters may be used in the optimality argument. Same parity alone
ensures the midpoint, not the whole segment. Equations (19)--(23) do
not claim that any intermediate point maximizes P_lambda.

For the exact body of Section 8 at lambda=1, all points in the segment
from x=1 to x=3/2 are active. The critical cap x>=1+t/2 has actual depth
2-t/2, its own root is 1+t/2, its remainder slab is (1-t)/2, and
Delta_t=0. Thus (22) is equality for every t; any finite increasing
subdivision also gives equality in (21) and (23). These sharp identities
again allow a whole same-base interval, so they provide no coverage or
finite-count conclusion by themselves.
